items.box: Modern street art comes in many different forms, and it makes cities colorful and lively. Today, we are going to see some well-known street artworks in London. The place ⓐ<u>that we are going to visit</u> is Shoreditch. Poor workers ⓑ<u>are used to live</u> in this area, but now it is one of the hippest areas in London. We can find so many great pieces of street art here. Do you see the painting over there? It is by the artist STIK. He is famous __(A)__ using only lines and dots in his paintings of human bodies. ⓒ<u>According to STIK, the three figures represents</u> the past, present, and future of Shoreditch. Which figure represents which? __(B)__, look closely at the eyes of the three figures. ⓓ<u>They are just dots, but they will give you a clue.</u> ⓔ<u>The eyes are so small that you can't see them easy.</u>

items.explain: 과거 노동자 거주 → 힙한 지역 → STIK 그림 → 눈에서 단서.

items.box: Kim Mandeok was born in Jeju-do in 1739. (A) She was a ⓐ[successful / terrible] businesswoman. (B) In 1795, she saw many people dying from hunger. (C) Her love for others was so ⓑ[selfish / selfless] that many people ⓒ[respected / ignored] her. (D) From her life, I learned that selfless love for others can make a big difference. (E)

items.explain: 성공한 사업가 / 이타적 사랑 / 존경.

items.box: We are now in Finsbury Park to see a painting by Banksy, an internationally famous street artist. Banksy's artworks often carry social messages, and the green tree you see over there is a good example. As you can see, he created a green tree by spraying green paint on a wall behind a leafless tree. Next to the tree, there is a person who is holding a sprayer. What message does Banksy want to give us through this painting? (A) <u>In many people's opinion, he is telling us that nature is having a hard time.</u> They think he wants us to take better care of it.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)에서 알 수 있는 Banksy의 그림에 담긴 태도로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: proud
worried
relaxed
excited
bored
items.explain: 자연이 힘든 시간을 보내고 있다 → 걱정.

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Banksy's artworks often carry social messages.
Banksy sprayed green paint on a wall behind a leafless tree.
There is a person holding a sprayer next to the tree.
Many people think Banksy wants us to plant more trees.
items.explain: 자연을 더 잘 돌보기를 원한다고 했다.

items.box:
On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield's house.
Man: Dr. Schofield, I have a special ⓐ<u>favor</u> to ask you.
Dr. Schofield: What can I do for you?
Man: Many people are going to gather tomorrow for the independence of Korea. Could you take pictures of the event and share them with the world?
At 2 p.m. on March 1, Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside. He began to take pictures.
Dr. Schofield: Unbelievable! There are so many people here. I hope the world will learn about this important event through my pictures.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ favor의 영영풀이로 옳은 것은?

a piece of writing on a particular subject in a newspaper
a written or spoken request for asking someone to come to an event
the group of people who officially control a country
an action that a group of people take to change something in society
items.explain: favor: 부탁, 호의.

items.stem: 윗글의 Dr. Schofield와 같은 방식으로 다른 사람을 도운 학생은?
choices: S 1: "I gave my old shoes to a homeless person in the subway."
S 2: "I took photos of the flood in my town and posted them online so people could send help."
S 3: "I fixed my neighbor's bike for free on the weekend."
S 4: "I taught English to children in my town every Saturday."

S 5: "I bought rice with my allowance and gave it to poor people."
(*S = Student)
items.explain: 사건을 기록해 세상에 알리는 방식.

items.box: On March 1, 1919, Dr. Schofield heard people shouting for Korean independence in Tapgol Park. He took pictures of the event with his camera. He then wrote an article about the historic event and sent it to foreign newspapers with his pictures. Dr. Schofield's fight for Korean independence didn't stop even after the March 1st Movement. He continued to write about the terrible situation in Korea for foreign newspapers. He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police, so he had to go back to Canada in 1920.

items.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: A Doctor Who Loved Taking Pictures
How Dr. Schofield Learned Korean
Dr. Schofield's Fight for Korean Independence
The Japanese Police in Tapgol Park
Why Foreign Newspapers Came to Korea
items.explain: 독립운동을 세계에 알린 투쟁.

items.stem: 윗글을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
items.box: Dr. Schofield took pictures of the March 1st Movement and sent an ⓐ___ to foreign newspapers. He ⓑ___ writing about Korea, so the Japanese police watched him and he had to ⓒ___ Korea in 1920.
items.explain: 기사(article)를 보냈고 계속 썼으며 1920년 한국을 떠나야 했다.

items.label: [17~18, 서답형1]
items.box: Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. He wanted to teach in Korean, so he began to learn Korean right away. (가) <u>그는 매우 열심히 공부해서 몇 년 만에 한국어로 가르칠 수 있게 되었다.</u> He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement. In 1958, he returned to Korea at the invitation of the Korean government and never left again. For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students. Dr. Schofield died in April 1970, and he was buried in Seoul National Cemetery.

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Dr. Schofield first came to Korea to take pictures.
Dr. Schofield learned Korean before he came to Korea.

The Korean government invited Dr. Schofield back to Korea in 1958.
Dr. Schofield left Korea again after 1958.
items.explain: at the invitation of the Korean government.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (가)를 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.

items.explain: so + 부사 + that + 주어 + 동사. 16단어.

items.stem: 다음 대화에서 A, B의 관계로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.box:

B: You can walk. Go straight for about 500 meters and turn left. It'll be on your right.
A: I see. How long will it take?
B: Only about 15 minutes.
items.explain: 길을 묻는 여행자와 길을 알려 주는 행인.

items.label: [21, 서답형2]
items.box:
B: Somi, I need help. What's the best way to get to Sebit Park from here?
G: Sebit Park? Well, you can get there by bus or by subway, but the subway is better.
B: OK. Which line should I take?
G: Take line 3, and get off at Sebit Station.
B: Line 3 and get off at Sebit Station. How long will it take?
G: It'll take about 40 minutes.
B: Is it that far?
G: Yes. Anyway, why are you going to Sebit Park, Liam?
B: Oh, there is an art fair this Saturday. <u>너도 원하면 나와 함께 가도 돼.</u>
G: Really? I'm free this Saturday. Let's go together.
B: Perfect. Let's meet here at 10.

②

< 보 기 > I know a girl. + Everyone likes her. ⇨ I know a girl whom everyone likes.
